text:
[NCBK.3.2] A metric emission is **self-describing**. One value carries
everything a receiver needs to route and fold the observation, with no prior
registration step and no schema to look up.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| name | the metric's dotted identifier, e.g. `ds.samples.dropped_total` |
| kind | how the receiver should fold `value` -- see below |
| value | the observation itself |
| labels / n_labels | optional dimensions; **`labels` is NULL whenever `n_labels` is 0** |

The kind is the field that decides aggregation: a **counter** contributes an
increment, a **gauge** replaces the previous reading, and a **histogram** is a
single observation the receiver buckets itself ([NCBK.3.3]). libds keeps
neither running totals nor bucket boundaries -- both live on the integrator's
side, which is what lets the one emission path serve stacks as different as
Prometheus and a plain array of counters.

Two consequences for a receiver. Because `labels` is absent rather than empty
when there are no dimensions, gate on `n_labels`, never on the pointer. And
because a single value field serves all three kinds it is floating-point, so
an integral counter delta is carried exactly only below 2^53.

The set libds emits is listed in [NMET.4.1] ([NCBK.3.4]). A receiver should
treat a name it does not know as a metric from a newer libds, not as an error.

The payload type is `ds_metric_t`, carrying `ds_metric_kind_t` and `ds_metric_label_t`, declared in `runtime/include/libds.h`.
